evidence.claim: The no-cache response directive requires a cache to validate the response with the origin server before using it to satisfy any subsequent request.
evidence.quote: RFC 9111 §5.2.2.4 defines no-cache as: the response “MUST NOT be used to satisfy any other request without forwarding it for validation and receiving a successful response”. Storing is fine.
evidence.title: Cache-Control: no-cache does not mean "do not cache" — By...
sub_questions: What is the formal definition of the Cache-Control: no-cache directive in the HTTP/1.1 specification?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states that a response with no-cache must not be used to satisfy another request without forwarding it for validation and receiving a successful response, which matches the claim.

evidence.title: Cache-Control: no-cache vs no-store
sub_questions: What is the difference between Cache-Control: no-cache and Cache-Control: no-store?
evidence.support_reason: The quote literally states that no-cache does not prevent storage.

evidence.claim: no-store is the directive that tells caches not to store the response
evidence.quote: no-store is the directive that tells caches not to store the response.
evidence.title: Cache-Control: no-cache vs no-store
sub_questions: What is the difference between Cache-Control: no-cache and Cache-Control: no-store?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states exactly that no-store is the directive that tells caches not to store the response.

evidence.claim: no-cache means a cache may store the response but must revalidate it with the origin before every reuse; no-store means do not store it at all
evidence.quote: TL;DR: no-cache means a cache may store the response but must revalidate it with the origin before every reuse. no-store means do not store it at all.
evidence.title: Cache-Control: no-cache vs no-store
sub_questions: What is the difference between Cache-Control: no-cache and Cache-Control: no-store?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states exactly that no-cache allows storage but requires revalidation before reuse, and that no-store forbids storage.

evidence.claim: Cache‑Control: no‑cache requires a cache to revalidate the response with the origin server before serving it
evidence.quote: no-cache: forces caches to submit the request to the origin server for validation before releasing a cached copy.
evidence.title: Cache-Control header
sub_questions: Does Cache-Control: no-cache require a cache to revalidate the response with the origin server before serving it?
